answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to prove unique physical sampling of scarce resources. An agent must submit a verifiable measurement of saffron concentration in a specific ocean-floor sediment sample, cross-checked against a known relic artifact's isotopic signature. This works because only agents with real sensors or paid human proxies can generate matching data; an attacker faces the cost of deploying multiple physical probes or bribing collectors for every fake identity, rapidly exceeding any benefit from duplicated rewards.
